utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar, if you could.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Before we start, we would like to thank to the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have the interpretation, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you hear me? Thank you. Before we start, we would like to thank the interpreters, the court reporters, and the technician supporters for their cooperation. Without their assistance, it was impossible for us to finish the testimony of that witness yesterday. We appreciate the effort they made to this end. As for today's scheduling of sitting, we were told we have to finish the sitting at 7.00 sharp. So we will divide this afternoon's sitting into three sessions; each will be 75 minutes. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please. I just want to remind you that you are still under the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Poriouvaev: [continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ajanic.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you all right today?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, better than the previous day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, let's hope for the best. The day before yesterday, Mr. Ajanic, we came to the point that while working at Hotel Ero, at one point you saw Drago Kordo, who informed you that your baby had died. My question will be what happened to you after you had heard about that incident?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing special happened. Because he knew me, he took me home for an hour or two, and then he brought me back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you returned to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did around 11.00, at night, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to you afterwards?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then they learned about it at the Heliodrom, and I asked that I be allowed to go and bury the child. They permitted me to go and be back by the morning. In fact, they said they would wait until the morning to see what would happen. So I was waiting to see whether they would let me go. They didn't. And I knew a soldier who was a member of the HVO, he was a policeman, and I asked him to give -- to provide me some tablets, some tranquilizers so that I could calm down because I was upset. He took me to the infirmary where there was a Bosniak Muslim prisoner who worked there as a physician. He gave me 50 milligrams of Apaurin and I took them all before dinner. And I did not know anything after that. I woke up in a municipal hospital. That's the next thing I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in hospital?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three months. And can I also ask if my sound can be turned up, the volume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question I would like to clarify. Did it all happen after the incident with Harmandic? I mean the death of your baby.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you released from Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the hospital. When I went to the hospital, they came several times to take me with, but the physician and a psychologist, Djurdja Faruk, did not allow it. But when I came to in the morning, the doctor asked me, Can you go to bury the child? And I said, Yes, of course. She said, Go in front of the office -- in front of the office there and wait for me to give you a release document so that nobody would touch you from the military. So I went home first to my wife. I asked what happened, and she said, Let's go up to Bijele Brijeg, that's where the child is. We went to the mortuary at Bijele Brijeg; however, we were told that he had been buried the day before. So I don't know to date where the child was buried. And then I went back home, had a cup of coffee, and then went back to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you released from hospital?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest with you, some three months later, and I was on a list of missing for a long time. But I only got papers from Zagreb some two months before coming to The Hague which certified that I was actually alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about three months, what do you mean? Do you mean from the moment you were taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment when I was taken to the hospital, I spent some three months in the hospital. And before that, I was at the Heliodrom for exactly three months and two days, imprisoned by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, and what happened to your second baby?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my second child is concerned, when they released me from the hospital, I came home and I asked my wife where Muhamed was, and she said, He is around somewhere. The other children were at home. They were told not to move about very much because we were of Bosniak faith. Several hours later -- I kept looking for him, I couldn't find him, and it was already dark. And the curfew was from 7.00 or 8.00, I'm not entirely sure. And then I saw a soldier, and I asked him, "Listen, have you seen my Muhamed anywhere?" He said, "I saw him. He was at Stela's." And he gave me a ride in his car to Stela's, and I was in the car. He went in and he told me this: "Halil, I would drive you further on, but one of my fellow soldiers was killed, so I can't take you there." However, in the morning when -- early in the morning, I went to Stela's, and I waited for him. He arrived with -- in a Jaguar, and I asked him, "Excuse me, Stela, do you know anything about my boy?" He said, "Come on over here to my office." We entered the office, and I just asked him, "Did he do something that he shouldn't have?" He said, "No, no, he did not. And do you want a coffee? Do you want something -- a stiff drink?" And it's true. And he said, "You know what happened to Muhamed?" I said, "I don't. If I did, I would not be asking you." He said, "Yesterday, he was watching television in a room with some Stela's soldiers. And apparently he had found a grenade and somehow activated it and was killed by it and was taken to the mortuary in Bijele Brijeg." And he was my favorite. I went to Bijele Brijeg to see him. I saw a man, a woman, and my son Muhamed whom I barely recognised because he was wearing boots which were of purple colour. I went to my wife to let her know. I did not have money so I did not know what and where. I didn't know where I would bury him. So I went to Stela, and I asked him, "I don't know what to do with him, how am I to bury him?" There was a man called Stipe Colak there. I know that he worked, for instance, something for the HVO. Stela asked him, Let's put him down as -- how shall I put it? -- as a casualty of war so that we would give him everything that he would be entitled to. And Stipe said, "I can't," and Stela said, "Please, see what the situation, he has no money." But Stela told me to go to the mortuary and to ask how much it would cost for a coffin and everything, all the other supplies. I had a neighbour whose name was Stanko, he used to be a driver before the war but at that point, he was something -- some kind of a boss there and he gave me a price, 180 German marks for the coffin, and this is what I came to Stela with. Stela gave me that money and I never repaid him. And Stela and Tuta were making a casino, and my sons and I worked quite a bit on that. We were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my objection is to the fact that the witness now has -- is speaking and testifying about events that occurred after -- well after -- the terms of this indictment, after January of 1994, and also the witness has gone on for some pages now without any direct questions being asked to him. I haven't objected to that. But at this point we're at a situation where the time frame has not been established, and I submit to Your Honours that the time frame of what he now speaks of is well after the terms of this indictment. And I object on those grounds, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, let us hear the story first. And when we evaluate all this evidence, we will take into consideration your objections. Witness, would you please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps you will allow me to ask the question, just to direct Mr. Ajanic to some certain points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, the day before yesterday, you informed the Trial Chamber that you worked for Stela, not only when you were a prisoner but later when you were not in prison. When --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, as a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And how did it happen that you, being a civilian, not arrested, were compelled to do the job?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: With all due apologies, Your Honour, that is a leading and suggestive question. It assumes facts not in evidence. And the word "compelled," I object to the form of that question, Your Honour. And again, until we establish a trial frame, I don't think it's relevant until it's determined to be within the scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is sort of leading, perhaps. You may rephrase your question and give us the proper time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to explain to you why I asked this question. First of all, in his testimony the day before yesterday, the witness explained that he performed forced labour for Stela, not only when he was a prisoner but later when he was not in prison. That's why I go on with his story. It's not my invention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I recall correctly, Your Honours, the witness did not mention any forced labour, and these are really sort of free interpretations of this. The witness did say that he worked for him, but I don't think that he ever said it was forced labour. So this is really misinterpreting what the witness had said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this is also true in this aspect so that we ask you, Mr. Prosecutor, to rephrase your question, and I can tell you we are eager to hear what the testimony of this witness is in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I rephrase my question. Did you work for Stela sometime later when you were released from prison? If you can recall, tell the Trial Chamber when it happened.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact information, but I worked on a casino as a free man. I was not imprisoned, and there were men who worked there because the Heliodrom was still operating, so there were prisoners there, too. I worked, as a rule, for money which I never received. And two of my sons also did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Ajanic, who invited you to work at casino?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stela's brother. He was nicknamed Marta. I don't know his given name, but it may have been his actual name. He ordered me 20 cubic metres of yellow cement, and -- sand, and he was -- that was to be done for 500 marks, which I never received. And otherwise, I was bringing in stones and cement, I loaded up debris and rubbish. And Mr. Tuta also came a number of times, and I wanted to approach him to ask him whether I could get some money but I could not go to him because he was always very busy and he always had five or six men around him and I was a little shy to approach him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, let's stop for the moment. Who else was involved in the work at casino? Do you see any prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I am objecting once again, for the record and for Your Honours, that the time frame of this alleged work that this witness has been speaking about was well after the term of this indictment, after -- well into 1994, and I believe the Office of the Prosecutor is well aware of that but they have failed and refused since my last objection to establish a time frame. And besides that, my other objection, Your Honour, is simply that it seems to me we're in an International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia concerning serious war crimes and now it almost sounds like we're in a civil courtroom, discussing a contract case of lack of payment of money. But I submit, Your Honours, in good faith that this incident of working for Mr. Stela was in 1995. And if I'm wrong, let my learned colleague tell me that. But if it is 1995, it is, I submit, wholly irrelevant and should not be heard. I appreciate your listening to me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, first of all, you have to establish the time frame of this incident. Secondly, we want to know whether it's within the time frame of the indictment or not. If it's out of the scope of the indictment, well, I'm afraid we'll reject this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can explain to you. First of all, the witness explained here that some prisoners from Heliodrom were involved in the job, and prisoners in Heliodrom were held until March 1994, so it was forced labour for prisoners of war, for prisoners held in Heliodrom. If we have continuation of criminal activities after the time frame, it doesn't deprive us of the possibility of leading this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: We submit, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, Mr. President. We submit that in the year of 1995, when this witness was working voluntarily for Mr. Stela, that there were still prisoners and people being held at the Heliodrom so it's still irrelevant. It happened, this occurrence is in 1995. And I believe the Prosecutor is well aware of that. And it's well outside the scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you have to ask the witness a question about the time frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, perhaps you will try to recall the time when it happened; 1994, 1995, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say only this: I cannot exactly recall it, but if I say -- if his Defence counsel says that in 1994 everybody was released from the Heliodrom, I can say this: Up until 1997, there were some people held in the underground hangar. And there were some prisoners there, and there were also some private prisons at Tuta's, and these people had their jaws broken there and things like that. I know that, and I guarantee that this was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think that I will not any further questions on this point because the witness tried and explained, to the extent he is able to explain, the situation of his participation in the construction of the casino.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer this precisely. I can say the precise location of the cafe and the tavern of Dubia where I worked. If I could only see the picture I would be able to explain it all, where they entered and how they entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I think that we will not need any further explanations. Thank you for that. And now I would like to return to some points in your previous testimony, just for the sake of clarifying your responses.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer? What I forgot to say earlier?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, I would like to ask some certain questions relevant to some definite points. Returning to the incident with Harmandic, explained the day before yesterday that you saw him on several occasions on that day. Did you manage to talk to him?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have opportunity to talk to him when we were unloading canned food. The name of the restaurant was Hladovina. He told me Halil, for me, this is the first and the last time. Nobody will ever see me again. While we were unloading those tin cans, Ernest Takac came by, and Dolma. He was nicknamed Dolma, and he hit Neno in the crotch. He fell, and Takac told him several times, "Get up, you old commie," and hit him in the crotch time and again. And then they left, and I was left alone to unload the goods because Neno was in too much pain from the blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it the only opportunity of talking to him on that day?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more point just: The day before yesterday, you mentioned a person Splico, and you also explained to the Trial Chamber that on one occasion, one lady, exactly Mujo Pupacic's wife, sent him to your home, and he mistreated you. First of all, I would like to clarify, when did it happen?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened when I had left the Heliodrom. Splico stopped my boy, whose name was Samir, down at the yard. And he told him, "You come with me." But the boy tried to resist, and I just happened to come out, and I saw him with his finger on the trigger, pointing his gun at the boy. And I came to him and grabbed the rifle, and he told me, "You come with me, then." I told him, "I can't, I am working for an HVO soldier whose name is Vili." My job was to clean their offices, and they paid me in canned food, flour, things like that. And he replied, "Let's go and see if that's true." So we went there, but there was no one there. Not Vili, not anyone. And he started hitting me. And I later learned that it was Mujo Pupak's wife who put him -- who informed him. And he was in the prison with me. When you entered, he was on the right-hand side, and Bosniak people were on the left. So I learned later it was Mujo Pupak's wife who put him up to it. I remember that I was on the left, upstairs. The other prisoners were on the other side, and the women were in the attic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, do you mean this same Splico that was held in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, my direct examination is over at this point. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Mr. Par. Before you start, I have to remind you that this witness is also a victim, and we can see that he is very nervous. So please conduct your cross-examination gently and politely. You may proceed, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will abide by your instructions. Cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ajanic.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Jelimir Par, one of the Defence counsel for Vinko Martinovic, Stela. I will be putting to you some questions regarding your testimony. To begin with, can you tell us if you have a nickname by which you are known in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Lopata," which in English means "spade."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get that nickname? How did it originate?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, you are standing up. I can't look at you. Those --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, it has to do with the manual labour you did; that you were a good worker?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, I would like to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the procedure in this courtroom is such that I am putting questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Something seems to be wrong with the record. My colleagues are pointing out to me that the previous answer of the witness has not been recorded regarding the origin of his nickname. The witness replied that it has to do with his ability to work well with his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was just telling you that there is a certain procedure here, and we should stick to it. So what was your occupation before the war? Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a manual labourer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in an enterprise or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for a single day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you work, then? Did somebody call you, offer you a job?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live in 1991?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar. That's where I was born. And seven years earlier, I lived in a place 15 kilometres from Nevesinje. The name of the place is Kljuna. That's where my wife is from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to Mostar then; 1991, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 when the Chetniks -- no offence meant to anyone -- came to Mostar, and I stayed there as long as the Chetnik war was on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. Were you expelled from Nevesinje or did you come of your own accord?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came of my own accord because I know what Nevesinje and the Kasaba of Nevesinjska meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were afraid of the war and the things that might happen to you and that was the reason why you came to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I came to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Mostar, how many family members were you in total?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were seven members of my family; myself, my wife, and one child was born during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you get settled in Mostar? Did you rent a place or find a house?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an old house. It had one large room, a corridor, and a kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it an abandoned house or what?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was owned by Meho Krhan, and I paid him, if you know the old bank notes, the Tito's 500 bill, that's what I paid him each month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll have to go slower for the sake of interpretation. I am being warned that interpreters are having trouble keeping up with us. Can you please tell me, what are you doing now for a living?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as before. The same as before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Opine 29, opine of Serbian faith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are living in a house which was Serb-owned?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is still Serb-owned, but I have to live somewhere. Beggars are not choosers. I was expelled, and I was caught during the war between the HVO and the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a formal decision allowing you to move into that house or what?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no decision whatsoever. The landlady came and said, "Halil, you may here as long as it takes for the house to be rebuilt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think that this question and the problem of the apartment is completely irrelevant to this case. And the question is quite redundant, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, would you please show us the relevance to the indictment about this witness's apartment. If not, would you please skip this set of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have one more question related to the previous testimony, and I hope it will elucidate the relevance which I believe exists. And if you would allow me, I would like to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, has someone, perhaps, of the local authorities - the police or anyone else - promised you that you would be allowed to stay in that Serb-owned house or that you would be given another place to live in Mostar after you testify in The Hague? Were there any conversations to that effect?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was talk that there was a humanitarian organisation which would repair my house in Nevesinje and I would be able to go back. Somebody else's home can never be your own home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you contact that humanitarian organisation? Did you do it personally or through official contacts?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are organisations, and you know it yourself, who offer money for 10, 15, 20, 30 houses to be rebuilt in a certain village. And in the place where my wife is from originally, the population is Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My point was, in order to exercise that right, did you gain any points by coming here to testify? Were any promises made to that effect?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no promises. It's just that Eso Tanovic nicknamed Prezle came and said, "Stela's father, called Mujo Tuta, is looking for you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this loan.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which loan?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the humanitarian organisation.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no loan, it's just that they're offering money. Every person whose house had been destroyed, if he cannot rebuild it himself, somebody else can be found to rebuild it. Otherwise, the person has to rent and become a subtenant again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us come back to your first arrival to the Heliodrom. You said that the first time you came to the Heliodrom, a list was made of all of you who arrived there, and all your personal effects were taken away, including shoelaces and trouser belts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, I wanted you, Mr. Par, to go back to the part -- it's incomprehensible to me what this witness was saying because you were talking over him, and the witness didn't get a chance to finish. So I think you should go back and ask him what you are asking about whether any promises were made to this witness in relation to his house if he testified here. And he was saying something about Eso Tanovic, nicknamed somebody. After that, it was incomprehensible. Could we go back to that, please. I think it's appropriate for you to ask those questions and not for us later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I asked you a moment ago about the way your accommodation is going to be dealt with. I asked you specifically regarding your accommodation. Have you been given any promises by officials somehow connected to your testifying in The Hague? You gave me a certain answer, and I'm now asking you to repeat that answer.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you: You have asked this question more than once whether anybody gave me a remuneration. What possible remuneration could there be when I don't have a penny to leave to my children while I'm away? I left Mostar without a single Deutschmark in my pocket. I'll stop testifying if you continue in this way. I'm not a thief. I'm an honest worker. You can see my hands. You can see the calluses on them. I do honest work to feed my wife and my children. I'd rather leave this courtroom than continue asking questions [as interpreted] in this vein. If you are doing this because you have to as an official of the Courts, aferim but if you are doing this for money, then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I don't want to upset you. I didn't mean to imply or to insinuate anything, but it is my job to ask certain questions. And I am asking you to take it in that spirit; namely, that I am just doing my job just as you have to do yours. And please, may I ask for your cooperation if we are continuing this examination. We may take a break if you need one, but there is no need for us to interrupt your testimony.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Defender, I could have gotten from his father 5, 10, 20, 50.000 if I accepted not to go, not to testify. But I didn't do that. I wanted to tell the truth. It weighed heavy upon me. And I'm telling you now I feel a load has come off my back. I want to stop this once and for all. One more word, and I'll take off my headphones and I'll go straight to the prison, if I have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see no way to continue this examination of this witness. I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to help me continue and finish with the questions that I have prepared for this witness. And I asked Trial Chamber's cooperation.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer if you give me half the money that you got. You keep mistreating me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we need a break at this moment, an early break, so that both sides could cool down and think of your strategy of the cross-examination during the break. Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness out of the first. We'll resume at quarter to 4.00. --- Break taken at 3.14 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, before you resume with this witness, I would like to say a few words to you. The first thing is that you have to ask your question very slowly and make a pause after hearing the answer from this witness, because the interpreters are having a very difficult time since your question and answer are always overlapped. Secondly, as I warned you before, you have to try your best to conduct your cross-examination very gently, fairly, and politely to this witness. You might remember that this Chamber has already said that whenever there is a dispute between the witness and the counsel from both sides, we will blame the counsel rather than the witness because you are professional. I know it's very difficult in certain situations, but you have to bear in mind that you are leading the witness rather than the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understood your warning and advice, and I really am trying not to create a situation in which the witness would polemicise with me. And I'm also trying not to hurt his feelings regarding the experiences that he lived through. However, on the other hand, I must be able to ask certain questions which I deem relevant and on which I have instructions from my client, and I am trying to do that in a way which would be the least irritating to the witness. However, let me add one more one: It is one thing how an attorney should work with a witness, but there are a number of witnesses here - and this may be a typical case - they come to answer to the questions posed by the Prosecution in the direct examination; and when the Defence's turn comes, they feel as if they have to come up with something new and shocking. And after they have done so, they refuse to cooperate. And the counsel finds himself in a very tough situation; that is, we are unable to conduct a proper cross-examination. So I would like to request that in the course of my further cross-examination, that the witness also be observed in terms of his being upset, upset either by my questions or in general, whether this is something that is prompted by the question or this is an attitude. I'm not trying to suggest or claim or accuse anyone of anything, but I invite the Trial Chamber to also pay attention to that aspect of the questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll talk to the witness in our own way. Yes, Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Before the witness comes in, can I just say something else. A new practice seems to be developing in this Court on the Defence bench, and that is that we can very clearly hear conversations which are taking place between the Defence counsel for Mr. Naletilic. We can hear every word; we can hear sighs, groans, and exchanges of views. I don't think it's appropriate. Possibly you don't realise how the acoustics work. But I really think that you should modulate your tone first, generally; and secondly that you should refrain from having disputes or conversations while the witness is actually giving evidence because it's very distracting to the translators and to us. I know it's not being done deliberately and towards the end of term we were all tired and things were getting a little more relaxed but let's do it differently, back to the way we were. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, let me say a few words to you: We understood that you are eager to help us, to give your evidence. We appreciate that very much. However, you have to remember that the purpose for you to come to The Hague is to help us, I mean the Judges, rather than to argue with anybody in this courtroom. You may not be familiar with the practice before this Tribunal, so you may answer the question very slowly and very clearly. There's no hurry. And before you, there is a monitor. Every word you said will be typed and will appear on the monitor. If you see the typing stop, you may answer the question. Thank you. Thank you very much for your understanding. You may proceed, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, please let us continue. During the break, I spoke with my client in regard of the contacts which you have mentioned as having had with his father and regarding his testimony. I asked Vinko Martinovic whether he knew anything about this and whether his father told him anything about this. Vinko Martinovic told me that his father said that a person came to him, Sead Kapetanovic, nicknamed Kapa, that he had come to him, asking on your behalf 10.000 German marks as a condition for your testifying in The Hague. My question to you: Is this correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guarantee, God forbid I can be brought back in a coffin to my children if this is so. And I don't even know this Kapa person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I see here only nicknamed Kapa, but I don't see the full name of the person who approached the witness, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par. You may make it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person's name is last name Kapetanovic, K-A-P-E-T-A-N-O-V-I-C. And the first name is Sead. S-E-A-D. The transcript, Yes, it is now reflecting it correctly, and he nickname is Kapa, K-A-P-A. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, we will move on and we will discuss the Heliodrom now. In your examination-in-chief, day before yesterday, if I remember correctly, you said that when you had arrived at the Heliodrom, you were all registered, that all your personal effects were taken away from you, and all the belts and shoelaces were taken away from the prisoners, too. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see that every prisoner was dealt with that way, but those of us who were taken to the prison. And that in front of the prison, they took our belts and laces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, you were assigned to clean rooms, to sweep.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the barracks, but not the areas where the prisoners were. The only thing that I did was took some cleaning supplies to the toilets, chlorine. And I was sweeping all the way on the perimeter from where the prisoners were to where the women were. And I also was sweeping on the perimeter. I also knew the man who was a driver in charge there. He was an ethnic Serb, and he had this Tam truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me who assigned you to these tasks?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Buhovac. And he said this: "Halil, it's better if you did this, because you'll have enough to eat and drink and nobody will mistreat you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is how it was. You had better conditions than the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can guarantee that with my life. I did give -- I shared my food, that is, my canned food and my bread, with other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Stela, you also did the same kind of work?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were also the easiest jobs in his unit?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was better to do whatever else than be at the front line. I was never with any army, I was never a member of any military. And on one occasion Stela told me, Halil, it's -- it's better that you do this than do what your little one did. That is, I knew this one young man who now would be 27 and who was with the army at the time when the HVO and the ABiH were still together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a special reason why you, Halil Ajanic, was spared these tough jobs? Did you have any friends with the HVO or something like that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: I was a friend with this same Stela before the war, and I could not believe that he could do something like this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the Heliodrom, this Buhovac who assigned you to these jobs, did he have any reason, did he have any interest to assign you to these easier tasks?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met him in the period between the Chetnik war and the war between the HVO and the Muslims. At that time, the Muslims and Croats were still together. And I was -- I did something for Kasim Redzic before the war. I was hauling some sand for him, for his house. And then he saw me at the Heliodrom once I got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay at the Heliodrom, did you collaborate with Buhovac or anybody else of the HVO in any way?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not collaborate in any way, but I did do whatever I was told to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were cases at the Heliodrom that some of these prisoners somehow collaborated with the HVO in some fashion?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have freedom of movement. I only worked and then went back to my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is this: You told us about Hamica, the Albanian, who told the HVO where Harmandic was. Do you remember when you said that during your evidence?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to look for 25 men, but they were looking for Neno Harmandic, whether he was there at the room, but Hamica, the Albanian, said, "I know where he is," and he went with the two Smurfs and they brought back Neno Harmandic and he was driven away in the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Hamica collaborate with the HVO and, in return, was given certain privileges?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, tell me, was that the first time you were in the prison when you arrived at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest with you, I was -- during Tito's reign, I served six and a half years in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us where you served the sentences?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Foca and Zenica. The first time, when I was to go to Foca, I was going to go to a mental institution. They diagnosed me as a mental patient, and I have been treated since the war, too, and my treatment has not been complete. And my diagnosed code is 303.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sokolac. Zivko Gruic was the head of the ward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was this, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I think 1974, 1975, but please don't take me by my word because I tend to forget, but I cannot forget the truth of what happened. I cannot remember dates and years. I don't even know when my son was killed. If you were to point a pistol at me, I still wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to burden you with such details, but please tell me this: Were you treated recently? I didn't quite understand you. You said that you were in treatment but the treatment is not completed.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at the hospital in the mental ward that I was treated, but that treatment has not been completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the release papers with you, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not bring anything with me. But you can call up this mental clinic in south camp in Mostar, and you can ask them whether this is true or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you know the physician's name?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it for sure, but I forgot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the reason why I asked you all these things, whether you had been in prison before, I wanted to know whether this experience -- previous experience had helped you sort of find your way around here or perhaps it was some acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had brought this sand for money. There were two truckloads of sand, a hundred marks per load, so those were 200 marks in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the Heliodrom, were there cases that some prisoners beat other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we got into fights among ourselves. You see that anywhere; it wasn't only at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally in a situation that you personally beat up somebody at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there cases, or perhaps did the HVO ask of you, let's say, Halil, go and beat up such and such person?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the Heliodrom, but at Stela's, yes. At his basement, I was told to beat up Harmandic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we'll come to that, but I asked you about the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, were some prisoners in fear of you? Were they afraid of you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they thought that I am informing on them, that I was passing information to the HVO. I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the prisoners fear that you might beat them?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we please go into the private session because I would like to mention a name which perhaps is better that it be told in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please. Mr. Par, I think you have to inform this witness what private session is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue now? I would kindly ask you, if you need a break because you're tired or for whatever reason, please tell me so. Can we continue now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Neno Harmandic whom we have been discussing for two days now, he, too, worked in the police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he personally ever take you into custody, arrest you, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why he did so?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For minor frauds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he beat you on those occasions, or mistreat you otherwise?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; he punched me in the heart once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- did you have a grudge against this Harmandic? Did you want to take your revenge on him?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did a little, and at Stela's quarters when they told me to hit him. But when I saw his condition, I couldn't really hit him. And I said I can't, I can't do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any reason, or do you have any reason now to feel vengeful about Stela?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were on good terms even before the war. I have no reason to wish to take any revenge. You can ask Stela himself about that time. As for later times, since the war, opinions have changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My point is this: Do you think perhaps that Stela is to be blamed for the death of your son? Do you blame him for that accident?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that this unfortunate incident took place on the premises in an apartment occupied by some foreign soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. And I know he was killed by a mercenary nicknamed Svabo [phoen]. He murdered him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think it wasn't an accident?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I know what this child meant to me. I know what he was like. He knew -- he knew about things that would happen tomorrow. He was considered to be the smartest child in the community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you know that it was precisely Stela who called the police and told them to arrest those foreigners?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I won't mention the name of the man who told me about this, but I was told by the man who had conducted the on-site investigation. I was told by him that this grenade was -- had been rammed into my child's mouth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the police, then, came on site, there was an investigation? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know all about that. But I also know that the child didn't put the grenade into his own mouth and then lock the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this apartment was located in relation to Stela's quarters?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Stela's quarters, that is Stela's tavern which used to belong to a Muslim from Nevesinje, and there was just one house between two places. It belonged to a man called Ribica, a taxi driver with a large family. This site now holds a building more luxurious than this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this place was occupied by foreigners?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, you blame Stela for this?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. 100 percent. First of all, if it was my child, as it was, Stela should have driven him away and told him, "You have no business being here," because it was an 8-year-old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Stela later had all those foreigners arrested, that he delivered them to the police, and that they were never members of his unit again?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you angry with Stela because of this money that has never been paid to you for the work you did at the casino?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me ask you: You would be probably angry if you missed one payment for one single hearing, let alone two months of hard labour you did together with your two sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you to mean that you are angry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perfectly correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was supposed to pay you for that work at the casino? With whom did you negotiate? Was it the people who were around at the casino or was it Stela?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Stela and his brother, Marta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever remind Stela that he hadn't paid you? Was he aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: I was to be paid 500 Deutschmarks for the two truckfuls of sand I had brought his brother. I was never given that money. And later, Stela invited me to clear up the premises of that building -- give me a minute to think. And he -- this Stela commissioned fine sand to be brought to the site, and the rubble to be cleared out. And he also ordered some prefab construction elements and mosaic stone for that building. You can ask him about all of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did. He said that that's true.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I swear by the grave of my late son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know when we are supposed to take the break. And if someone could possibly remind me so that I can plan the rest of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll sit until 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us go back to that moment when Harmandic was brought to the office where you were together with Stela at that moment. If I remember correctly, you said that it was Takac who brought him? He said that Harmandic had tried to escape and Stela said take him to the basement and don't beat him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ernest Takac addressed him as, "Comrade General."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking about generals, was Stela wearing any signs of rank?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was found unfit to serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague is pointing out to me that the record is not quite correct. You said, "Comrade General."

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man said this guy Neno Harmandic had tried to escape. Neno said, "I didn't, Stela, I promise." But Stela replied, "Take him downstairs and don't beat him." However, when he was taken away, I was still downstairs --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have some problems. It seems to me that we have some questions and answers mingled together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see what the problem is, and I'll try to clarify it once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you, did he address him as "Comrade General"?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He addressed him as, "Comrade, General."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was Ernest Takac who addressed him this way?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That used to be the form of address accepted formally in the former Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do me a favour. I don't know about these things because I never did my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After a while, is it the case that Stela left with this Mujo to take him -- to take a bath or something? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mujo Tuta confirm to you that he had been taken by Stela to take a bath at his house?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And also to do some repair work on his car, because Mujo Tuta was a mechanic. He did, indeed, have a bath, and when he came back, he was dressed in a totally new set of clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else together with you in that office at the moment when Ernest brought Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just Stela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us revert to the incident when those soldiers told you to hit Harmandic. Did you hit him once, at least?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single time, when I saw what condition he was in. But before that, Harmandic told me himself, "Halil, hit me, hit me. You have a lot of children to think of, and I'm finished anyway. I'm a goner." And the soldiers had told me, "Lopata, you give him a bit of a beating, too. If you don't, you'll get a beating yourself."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, did you later hear at the Heliodrom that the story circulated among prisoners to the effect that you had beaten Harmandic? Have you ever heard about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard there was a story like that. And I have witnesses to confirm that I didn't, nor would I ever hit a man when he was down. On the contrary, I would try to help him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, fine. Who told the prisoners at Heliodrom the story of what really happened concerning Harmandic? Was it yourself?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was I and Mujo Tuta. There could have been no one else. Maybe some stories were told by one soldier to another, and then it was picked up by soldiers who served at the Heliodrom, you know how these things go. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 7578 to 7597 Maybe somebody said that Lopata had helped in the beating. Every army - and it was my father who told me this a long time ago - has its informants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is still true that you told this story to the other prisoners at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not afraid of the truth ever. There is a God above me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because we have already heard the testimony of many other former prisoners who confirmed that you had told them this story, and specifically there was a Witness U who was here on the 25th and the 26th of December [as interpreted]. He said that it was he who had saved your life after you had taken those pills, and he told us that you told the story of this incident to the other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what happened to Neno Harmandic? Yes, yes. I certainly did. That much is true. First of all, you can ask Stela himself whether I beat that man. He will tell you, and then you may also ask him whether he had told me to beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we have already mentioned this Witness U who saved you before you went to the hospital in this incident with your suicide attempt, tell me, was it really an attempt to take your own life, to poison yourself, or what?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a suicide attempt, an attempt at poisoning, because it was all the worst. My wife had gave birth to nine children, some of them died, were killed - God bless my late Muhamed - and you should go and see what condition the rest of my children are in. And when I was leaving my home to come here, she fell to the ground -- she fainted, she was so weak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a suicide attempt?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are moments when you wish that you no longer exist, and when you have a child, all you wish is to hold him and to cherish him, and then they leave too soon to the heavens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, do you know anyone from this family Harmandic? Have you ever seen any one of them or talked to them?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, with his son. And I told him the same story I'm telling you here now, and I swear that it is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when was it, approximately, when you talked to him?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It wasn't once that I talked to him. It was perhaps 30, 40 times that I did that. And I'm going to go on to say this to anyone, what happened and what his death was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His son works for the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he is the same as his father was, and this is why I say whatever goes around comes around. And you know, whoever -- it could be a policeman or an agent or something like that. And there is Stela, but from Stela -- from his son, two Stelas develop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the interpretation. Did you talk to Harmandic's son at the police because he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the street?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First off, he never put on a uniform, and I don't know if he is a policeman. It is -- but he can only be what his father was or what his uncle was because his father -- he, too, worked in plainclothes. And I think you should just stop asking me these questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you're tired --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can go on like this for five days, but it is all useless. I'm answering everything you're saying. I'm being polite to you, and I'm saying everything in a truthful way, and I swear I will go on telling the truth until the end. But with all due respect, this is all provocative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can I ask to take a break now so that I can consolidate my questions and then I'll be finished.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can we just please go on so that I can be done and then I can have the burden lifted off my shoulders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have made an order that we will break at 5.00. There's only about 10 minutes to go. Mr. Par, would you please continue for another 10 minutes; then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to Harmandic's wife?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the police ask you -- question you about this Harmandic incident?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the police, but those who did were -- how shall I call them? It wasn't the police. I don't know if it was the state security or that service for the missing. I can't explain this. But I did talk to the people who really were in charge of that for the casualties of war. I think that that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the AID? Do you know what AID is?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The AID is some kind of a secret service of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. You know what, it could be Jesus Christ, but I still wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what I'm trying to ask you: First of all, I'm trying to ask you whether these police talked because I want to see whether the police suspected you of having been involved in the beating of Harmandic.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me? No. Not me. But who knows? Maybe they even thought that I did. Who's to know? But the truth remains the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I mean: When Stela told me that my child was killed, I wanted to kill him. But I would have lost all my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your evidence, you said that the last time you saw Harmandic he was alive?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was alive, covered with boards in a canal. And the police was -- they were filling buckets with water and pouring it over him through the boards. And as we were starting off to the Heliodrom, I saw as they placed him in that canal alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally never saw him again?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never laid my eyes on him again. I only heard that at the Sarajevska bank, that he was transferred there to the square near the HIT department store. And from there -- he was dead then. Then he disappeared, and nobody knows where he is buried. Or perhaps he is even alive, but I have not seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a second so I can confer. Mr. Ajanic, in closing, let me just ask you this: Are you in treatment? Do you receive any medication now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go ahead, tell us.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am taking aspirin, .3, to calm down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any other medication in recent days?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only missed one pill the day I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague has asked me, was it aspirin or Apaurin; what did you take?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apaurin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this completes my cross-examination, and I thank you, Mr. Ajanic.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. And don't forget, I'm a little man, but I'm still strong-minded [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Naletilic considers that our learned friends have exhausted the questions and we will ask no additional questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's almost 5.00 at this moment, so shall we break now at this point? I saw everybody nodding. Mr. Usher, would you take the witness out of the room first. We'll resume at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to inform the Chamber that, during the break, we had a correction in the record. Page 42, line 21, there was the witness's comment. We believe that the witness said something completely different; not that he was a little man, but in Bosnian what he said is a word that is very similar sounding but it means something akin to crazy, mad. I consulted with the interpreters. The interpreters did acknowledge the error. I have also discussed it with the OTP, as did the interpreter. So now I'm just laying it out before the Trial Chamber and want to know whether we should consider this now as a corrected transcript or shall we recall the witness to deal with this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that we should leave it to the interpreters, and they will check it all and perhaps they will inform us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, thank you very much for informing us about this correction in the transcript. But we still have the witness with us. For the fairness to the other party and to this Trial Chamber, if you have some problems with the translation in the transcript, you may have another opportunity to ask this witness about what he said, rather than directly approaching to the interpreters to have it corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, with permission of the Chamber, I'm going to direct that question again to the witness, even though I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Bring the witness, please, Mr. Usher. Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry we have to keep you a little bit longer in this courtroom. Yes, Mr. Par. Further cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ajanic, I have no further questions for you, but with the permission of the Trial Chamber, I'm going to try to resolve with you something that I think was entered in error in the transcript, and I would like to -- like you to tell me whether I'm right or not. It is something that you said just before you left the courtroom. As I understood it, you said, "I may be crazy but I still have my wits around me." Can you tell us exactly what you said?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I said. I have a paper to prove that I am crazy but I am still lucid enough and my mind is still together enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ajanic, and thank you, Your Honours. I think that we have resolved this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: To Mr. Ajanic. Re-examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I just want to clarify one situation. You explained to the Trial Chamber that at some point, Harmandic was put in some canal and soldiers took buckets and poured him with water. I would like you to describe that canal. What do you mean by "canal"? Because "canal" is a very broad notion.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you. This is like a canal, like a pit in a garage. They placed him in it and, on top of him, they placed boards. But to the left, there was a hose, and there was a tap there. And they poured water in this plastic thing that kids are bathed in, and then they said, "Neno where are you?" and he said, "I'm here," and then they poured water in that direction from which the voice came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question will be: During the cross-examination, you mentioned the person whose name is Miro Kolobara. Did you know Miro Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is now driver for Cash, and I did not know him before then, from before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him during the war?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, towards the end of war, when Mujo Pupak was at the Heliodrom and when he came with his daughter to bring him bags with food or change of clothes or something. And she, too, was wearing an HVO uniform. Then later on, I saw him in his own house, that is, in the house of Mujo Pupak, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Miro," is it a real first name? Does this name exist in your language, "Miro," or is it a shortened name?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a name does exist, and the last name "Kolobara" does exist, too, so it's not shortened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recall that that name and that person were ever brought up in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was brought up in the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please show us where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, it is just talking about some secretary, Mr. Kolobara, and this secretary was a relative of some Pupak or something like that. We have it. I'm sorry, I don't have it just on the monitor now.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he said that he was afraid that I would see him --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's page 45 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Speak to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: 45, line 18. I don't invent things here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not trying to invent either, but I never mentioned that name because I'm not interested in that person. I don't even know who it is. I allowed that the witness, in his open-ended narrative, did mention this, but it was never a subject of my cross-examination. And I have nothing else to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The Prosecutor said you mentioned the person whose name is Miro Kolobara, which means that the witness mentioned that name. He did not blame you in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Page 29 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, procedurally, I think the witness was just called back to verify one word he said in a sentence that he gave that was not even to a question, and I don't believe it's proper for any further cross-examination or redirect examination. He was just brought back to explain one word. He wasn't asked a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I have been always taught that it was allowed during the redirect. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, my learned friend just asked you if it was the fact that a person with a nickname "Kapa" approached you and tried to encourage you to testify before the Trial Chamber for money. Could you tell me if there was anyone else --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to try to be very accurate about what I had asked so that we have a clear record. I said that my client, Vinko Martinovic, during the break, when asked, told me that the person nicknamed Kapa - Sead Kapetanovic, that is - had come to his father, asking for 10.000 German marks on behalf of this witness here in order for him not to testify here against him. That is, that this person Kapetanovic had asked, on his behalf, the money of Vinko Martinovic, and this is what I confronted the witness with. I think that that is what I had asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this respect, we would like to make an order. During the cross-examination, at least on three occasions, namely, line 22 of page 16; line 17 of page 18; and the third line of page 22 in the transcript, the witness mentioned the alleged attempts of offering some money for him to come to testify -- or not to testify before this Tribunal.
