We Judges deliberately avoid asking any questions in this regard, taking into consideration of the main subject of the cross-examination as well as the personal conditions of the witness. This Trial Chamber now orders the witness remain in The Hague for another day and the Prosecutor take sworn statements on those alleged incidents with the presence of the representative from the Registrar. And this Trial Chamber further orders the statements be submitted to this Trial Chamber. It is so decided. So you may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I will abide by your ruling. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I have a few issues that I would like you to clarify, please. You told us that you knew Mr. Neno Harmandic for about 20 years before the war, and you described to us that he used to investigate frauds and thefts and, I think, robberies. Was he what we would call a detective, a plainclothes detective?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. He never wore a uniform. And we called people like that agents in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Was he an agent or a detective during the Tito regime?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And after the death of Mr. Tito, did he continue, right up to the war, being an agent?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, when you were in the prison at the Heliodrom, were you aware that Mr. Harmandic was also a prisoner prior to the day that you are talking about, the day where you believe he was killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So can I understand, so we're perfectly clear about it, that the first day you met him in the prison was the day on which you believe he was killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You also described how two brothers - who I think the pronunciation I heard was brothers called Smurf - were looking specifically for him.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were looking specifically for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you know who these brothers Smurf were?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know it at the time. I learned later that those two Smurf brothers were the children of Ivan Culo, who did the same sort of work that I did. He was a carriage driver and later he became a truck driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Is there any significance to Mr. Harmandic's fate in the fact that these two Smurf brothers were the children of Ivan Culo? Was he arrested or imprisoned by any investigation conducted by Mr. Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Was it your impression that when Mr. Harmandic became aware that he was being sought, that he was afraid, and is that why he hid himself?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you speak to him or observe him in the truck on the way to where you had to work that day? I think you said that you went to Stela's.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was on that truck, but nowhere near me. I didn't see him. He was the last to get on the truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, if I bring you back to when you were in the building which you called Stela's, and you described to us what Ernest Takac said about Mr. Harmandic, I think you said that he said -- Mr. Stela said take Harmandic to the basement but don't hurt him.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: How long after that command did you hear the screaming?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three minutes later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And I know this is difficult and it's many years ago, but can you assist me on this: How much time went by before you heard the screaming and when you were called down into the basement? When you described that the soldiers called, "Lopata, come down here," and that Mr. Stela was in the basement, how long elapsed from between when he was taken first to the basement and when you were called down?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it may have been half an hour or an hour. I'm really sorry, I can't give you an accurate estimate. But somewhere around that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's very helpful because I wanted to know whether you were talking about two or three minutes or a period. So you think it could have been between half an hour and an hour. And that is helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, may I say just one thing. Three minutes after Stela said, "Take him downstairs and don't beat him," the screaming started. Half an hour or an hour later, they called out to me, laughing, "Lopata, come over here." And Stela was among those people. He told me, "Come on, hit me, or you'll get the same treatment."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You described afterwards how Stela left with another prisoner to allow him to have a bath, and he came back later. During that period, was Mr. Harmandic moved from the basement?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, to wash the car and - excuse the expression - two or three men urinated in a beer can and then gave it to Neno to drink. And one of those put him -- put his thing in his mouth and asked him, "Do you like this?" And Neno answered -- and he answered, "Yes, I do," but that was under duress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Judge Liu has sought clarification through me of something you said a few minutes ago. When you said that the soldiers were laughing and they said -- I'm reading the transcripts -- "Lopata, come over here," and Stela was among those people. And you said, "He told me, 'Come on, hit me,'" it says in the translation. Should it be -- what should that be? "He told me, 'Come on...'" Who told you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stela told me, "Hit him," and I said, "I can't. You can do with me what you like, but I can't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. And the reason that we asked you that question again and it's not that I want you to go over the evidence, it's that on the translation on the transcripts, it was,"Hit me," but what you're saying now is that he said, "Come on, hit him," meaning Mr. Harmandic. So if --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Harmandic himself said, "Halil, come on, hit me, hit me, you have a lot of children to think of, and I'm a goner anyway." And before that, Stela ordered me to hit him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can return to my previous question, when Mr. Harmandic was taken out of the basement and you described the incident with the soldiers and the empty cans of beer, forcing him to drink urine and the other outrages, can I take it that Mr. Stela was not there at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't there with them. He had taken Mujo Tuta to have his bath and to repair his car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When Mr. Stela came back, where was Mr. Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was back down in the basement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I want to say to you that I'm, as a Judge, very impressed by your willingness to come here and use your own name and not ask for any witness protection. We're very impressed by that. There's just one last question that I want to ask you. You said that you have been treated for a psychiatric condition for a number of years. Do you know what your psychiatric condition is? What are you being treated for?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you in all honesty, since I had a great misfortune, article 255, embezzlement of social property, and I could have served 5 to 15 years under Tito's rule for that. But the psychiatrist, Dr. Herceg, who knew my father, helped me, helped me to get a different sentence; that is, to be sent not to prison but to a mental institution, and that way, they couldn't give me more than three years. And you have your own psychiatrists and you can ask them if what I am saying is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I don't for one moment question what you are saying, Mr. Ajanic. I just wondered as you are being treated on an ongoing basis at the moment, I can possibly guess what your condition is, but has your psychiatrist ever told you the name of the condition for which he is treating you? Is it, for instance, anxiety or post-traumatic stress or schizophrenia or depression or any of the other well-known psychiatric conditions? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: Tendency to aggression, that's what it is. And in the conclusion, it says that I tend to get out of control when I see a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge Clark's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions. I just want to check one thing in the transcript. As far as I can see, the one part of the witness's answer was not recorded. The witness mentioned considerably diminished responsibility from time to time, sporadically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my diminished ability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate your effort very much. We all wish you good luck in your future. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I say one thing in conclusion, seeing how I'm here already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You may rest assured - I'm a man who had never been on a plane before - but I came here to tell the truth. You may rest assured that everything I said is the truth. And if I had any fears, I wouldn't have come. And I would have certainly not spoken in public. I would have at least asked for some measure of protection, and I know, now that I come back to Mostar, there may be some trouble or something, but I'll try to deal with that. And I would still like to ask my question of the lawyer, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me talk to the witness first. Witness, we appreciate very much about your courage and about your cooperation for coming to The Hague to help us, the Judges. As a rule of this Tribunal, it is the Defence counsel who are entitled to ask you the questions, and you are in the position to answer those questions, unfortunately. I hope you could understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand very well. And I am very glad to have met you all, and I apologise, but I have to tell you that I have a long memory and I remember a lot of things. When I first came into this courtroom, however, and when I saw Stela, I couldn't remain calm and indifferent. Thank you anyway for letting me speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender through this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender the only document that I have. That is Exhibit P15.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it's about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It's Stela's office, as described by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It is admitted into the evidence, but I believe that this photo has already been admitted. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is already admitted. It was admitted on the 18th of September 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any documents to admit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None whatsoever, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, we are ahead of schedule, about 50 minutes early. Tomorrow morning, we will hear another witness, or are you ready to call another witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We are prepared to proceed with the next witness, Mr. President, who is an expert witness. And I think that it would be our preference to continue until 7.00, as scheduled, if the Trial Chamber is willing to do that, and the interpreters and the other technical people as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, is this a witness that we ought to have a report in front of us for?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I believe that they should be with you already, in a blue binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures that you are going to ask for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, I believe that the last information given to the Trial Chamber was that he was requesting protective measures, but that is not the case. The witness, Dr. Zujo, will testify in open session. And Mr. President, with your permission before the witness enters he courtroom, I perhaps could make just a couple introductory remarks about the witness, the expert witness report which is on the Bench under rule 94 bis and perhaps inform the Trial Chamber of the specific parts of the indictment which are relevant to the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness is Dr. Hamza Zujo. He is being called by the Prosecution to offer expert testimony pursuant to Rule 94 bis. The Trial Chamber may recall that, pursuant to that Rule, the Prosecution submitted a statement or a report of Dr. Zujo to the Trial Chamber. It was filed on the 19th of October of last year. And pursuant to a decision issued on the 27th of November last year by this Trial Chamber, you found the statement to be relevant and admitted the statement at that time. Subsequently, counsel for the accused Vinko Martinovic requested permission to cross-examine Dr. Zujo, and the Prosecution had no objection to that. And so now, Dr. Zujo is present and is prepared to testify before the Trial Chamber today. What we have done is to mark Dr. Zujo's 94 bis statement, which was previously admitted pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision. We have given it a number, 877.1, and that is the report that is on the Bench. And the report refers to a variety of documents which are attached to it, marked and tabbed individually. I should add that one of the documents, it's the document K which is in your binder, is not referred to in Dr. Zujo's report. The annexes are generally the report and findings made by Dr. Zujo and his colleague, Dr. Dobraca, concerning exhumations and autopsies which are of relevance to this case. Each of those is contained in the binder in English, French, and the original language, B/C/S. The final one, we did not have it in French at the time that the report was filed with the Registry, and subsequently, then, the last of the autopsy reports was received by us in French translation, so we have simply added that, and it is the last document in this binder, which is marked as annex K. It has never been previously marked and so we gave that a separate exhibit number, which is 877.2. But we will tender those at the conclusion of Dr. Zujo's testimony. Mr. President, this testimony is relevant to count 1, the persecution count, paragraph 27; it's also relevant to counts 2 through 8, specifically paragraph 42, which relates to the death of a person named Aziz Colakovic who is alleged to have been killed while being used as a human shield on the Bulevar; and finally, the evidence is relevant to counts 13 through 17, paragraphs 51 and 52, which relate to the killing and/or serious bodily injury inflicted to Nenad Harmandic. I will add that the third of the three autopsy reports which Dr. Zujo will refer to relates to his examination of the body of a person identified as Mustafa Krilic. Mr. Krilic is not mentioned in the indictment as a victim, however, there has been testimony about Mr. Krilic that has come in from other witnesses during the course of the trial. So we therefore felt that we should bring this autopsy report to the attention of the Trial Chamber or to include it within the testimony of Dr. Zujo. And so with that, Mr. President, I'm ready to proceed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: One question I want to ask you is that are there any English translations for Document J, K, in the binders we received?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Document J, K?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Document J and K.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have been more clear. The last three documents, Mr. President, are the autopsy report regarding Mustafa Krilic. So that document I is the document in English, Document J is the same document in B/C/S, and annex K is the same document in French. So although we have annexes going through K, it's actually less documents than that. We have just submitted three autopsy reports, each in three languages. So that A, B, and C are all the autopsy report of Harmandic in the three languages, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm going to lodge an objection on the part where Mustafa Krilic documents, that is, his autopsy documents are offered in record and Dr. Zujo's report. We believe that this is not part of the indictment, it is outside the scope of the indictment, and the reasoning that my learned friend, Mr. Stringer, has just offered now is insufficient. And on the basis of that, we cannot go into the issues that are outside of the scope of the indictment and bring in this autopsy through the back door and create certain impressions that may be damaging to our clients. I think that this is not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I absolutely agree with my learned friend Mr. Par, and in addition, I have to say that if my learned friend was going to bring in the autopsy of Mr. Krilic, he at least should have let the Defence counsel know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm disappointed with the objections for these reasons: First of all, the Krilic autopsy report was attached to the 94 bis statement of Dr. Zujo that was filed with the Registry and provided to the Trial Chamber on the 19th of October. So there's no surprise now about where we intended to go. The Defence has known since the 19th of October that we were including the Krilic autopsy report among the other two. That's number one. Secondly, neither accused filed any response or objection to the 94 bis statement when we filed it. Under the Rule, the Defence can either file an objection, in which case the Trial Chamber can rule on it, or they can not file an objection. Neither accused filed any response. And it was on that basis that the Trial Chamber admitted the statement into evidence in its decision of 27 November. Now, it turned out that one of the accused, in fact, approached the Prosecution and then the Trial Chamber and apologized, indicating that they had wanted to or had intended to file a response, had not done so within the time limits imposed by the Rule and asked, first of all, the Prosecutor whether we would oppose their request to bring the witness here for cross-examination. I think Mr. Scott did the right thing and the fair thing, which was to agree that they could cross-examine the witness if they wanted to, but in fact, they are not even entitled to this cross-examination today if one construes 94 bis literally, which is to say no objection was filed. And under the letter of the Rule, the statement comes in and serves as a substitute for the testimony of the expert. And that's very well where we could be today, had not the Prosecution agreed to not oppose the Defence request to bring the witness for cross-examination anyway, even though they didn't file any timely objection. So I am disappointed to hear an objection today about the scope of the expert report when, number one, it has always included reference to the Krilic autopsy report; and secondly, since the Prosecution felt that it was being flexible, fair, and considerate to the Defence by even agreeing to allow the witness to come, be subject to cross-examination today when, in fact, the witness might never have had to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, can I say something first before anybody objects. First of all, can I direct the same remark to you that I addressed to Mr. Krsnik yesterday. It is counsel's place to make submissions to the court and not to express personal feelings of disappointment or generosity. If the evidence in this case, as with this witness, as has been submitted by Mr. Par, is outside the scope of the indictment, are you saying that the failure on the part of the Defence to raise appropriate objections at the time validates your attempt to introduce evidence which is not relevant? I would like you to argue that. It seems to be what you are urging on the court, that we are to disregard the admissibility or otherwise of this aspect of the witness's evidence because of the failure on the part of the Defence to act appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Judge Clark, I failed to add the other part of what I had intended to add, and forgive me if I got a bit carried away. When I informed the Trial Chamber of what we view to be the relevant parts of the indictment, I mentioned paragraph 27 of count 1, which alleges that between April of 1993 and until at least January of 1994, thousands of Bosnian Muslim civilians were interned in detention centres under HVO authority in the area of Mostar and the neighbouring municipalities. Beatings, torture, killings were common and persistent in these detention facilities. Now, it's our view, Your Honours, that the killing of Krilic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Stringer. "Our view" is not appropriate. "We submit." Because what's sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander. We're personalising arguments a little bit too much there. The Prosecution submit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We submit, Judge Clark, that the autopsy findings and information which is already in the record in respect of the killing of Mustafa Krilic, which occurred at the Dubrovkovici school detention facility is relevant to the allegations contained in paragraph 27 of count 1, which is the persecution count, although we acknowledge that he is not named -- a named victim whose name appears in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When did the Prosecution first become aware of the existence of this particular autopsy report?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It was -- I became aware of it before -- certainly before the trial. I don't know when this was disclosed to the Defence. But it, on the other hand, was, I can say I believe, not known to us at the time of the original indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, do you want to add something to your argument?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, not to belabour it very much. Her Honour Judge Clark actually did most of my work here. On a personal note, I want to say that we have on a number of occasions expressed our gratitude for the things that the Prosecution have done so far in this trial. And I do not want to appear that the Defence counsel is unfair, that we have received certain help, and we do not reciprocate. Our objection is a principled one. We cannot be expected, because we are in a situation that we have been given a favour by the Prosecution, that we are now going to depart from certain principles. We appreciate very much everything that the Prosecution have done for us, but we have to say that this goes outside of the scope of the indictment, and that is the principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there should be an end of this argument. Since we have the witness waiting outside the room, and we have very limited time this afternoon, namely about 30 minutes, shall we proceed with this witness on the other two autopsy reports at this moment, pending the decisions of this Trial Chamber at a later stage. Do you agree? Thank you. I saw everybody is nodding. Mr. Usher, will you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sorry for keeping you waiting for so long.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Stringer, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, good evening. Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, how you are currently employed. What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: I work at the Institute for Forensic Medicine in Sarajevo at the University of Sarajevo. I am a specialist for forensic medicine, and I also work on the teaching staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long have you been working in the field of forensic medicine?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Since 1977. That is when I started working for the Institute for Forensic Medicine, and that is how long I have been involved in forensic medicine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber just briefly a bit about your educational background and the training which led to your becoming associated with the Institute for Forensic Medicine.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: After I graduated from the medical faculty, I, in fact, showed affinity for forensic medicine, so I expressed my desire to specialise in forensic medicine, and then I did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what year you graduated from the medical faculty?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand correctly that at that time, then, you were a medical doctor?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you attend -- where did you undertake your medical studies?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: It was at that medical faculty at the University of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then did you pursue a more particularized course of studies that would have led to your specialisation in forensic medicine?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. After I graduated from the medical faculty, I spent a certain amount of time until I met the conditions to enrol in the forensic medical studies. And that took four years. And then I did do a specialist exam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you now also do some teaching. How long have you been teaching at the university?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes. And I have been doing it since 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having specialised in forensic medicine, have you ever obtained any certifications which have come from the court or the judicial system in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I asked the question poorly. Are you a court-approved or a court-certified forensic specialist such that you would testify in judicial proceedings in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies. I had not understood. Yes, I am a sworn court expert. In all cantonal and county courts, I appear as an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you held this authorisation or this certification to appear in court proceedings as an expert in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: I do it on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your duties as a forensic physician, and as a certified court expert, do you participate in exhumations and also in autopsies to determine causes of death?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Immediately after the end of the war, my institute became engaged in these exhumations and autopsies of remains so that, ever since the war, I have been continuously involved in exhumations and autopsies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber, please, the areas or the regions within Bosnia-Herzegovina in which you've participated in exhumations during the post-war period.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: My first exhumations were in the region of Sanski Most, Kljuc, and in Bosanski Petrovac. Then in the area of Travnik, that was in the Central Bosnia canton, and then it was in the Mostar canton. And...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then following up on exhumations, did you conduct autopsies, that is, examinations of bodies that were exhumed, in order to attempt to determine identification and also cause of death?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: My task was to supervise exhumations from the moment these sites were identified, to oversee their transportation all the way to the autopsy tables, and then to be involved in the autopsies themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after the conclusion of autopsies, did you then, were you involved in the making of reports, reporting of your findings, and the presentation of those findings to the judicial system within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: After the exhumations and the forensic processing, our written findings went to the courts that had requested these exhumations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, can you give the Trial Chamber a rough estimate of the number of exhumations, perhaps the number of autopsies, that you've conducted in your capacity as a forensic court expert in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: In any case, over 1500.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in exhumations and in autopsies of persons -- or I should say exhumations that occurred in the Mostar area -- I know you've already said Mostar. Did these exhumations occur during the period of 1998?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes. My institute received an order from the Mostar county court so that the team consisted of Dr. Dobraca and myself and our staff went out and conducted these forensic processing in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the name of Dr. Dobraca, and perhaps we should discuss who he is briefly, because I know his name is going to appear on a number of the following documents that we'll discuss. Can you tell us a little bit about who Dr. Dobraca is and the extent to which you worked with him in the course of these exhumations and autopsies.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Dr. Dobraca also worked at the Institute for Forensic Medicine, and he is also involved in teaching. He is a specialist in forensic medicine, and I can also say that we were -- we have worked -- we worked together in the Neretva canton on exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, I would like to hand the witness what has been marked as Exhibit P877.1, which is in a bound blue booklet. I don't think we'll be using the ELMO, at least not for a little while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, I would just like to ask you, if you could, take a look at this document. The first part of it is in the English language. Could I ask you to turn to page 9 of that document. Tell us if you recognise your signature on this document and tell us basically what this document and the attachments consist of.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature. And it is -- relates to the exhumations which we did in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to refer you to individual documents that are attached to this report, Dr. Zujo, but can we say that the attachments consist largely of your findings in respect of certain autopsies that were performed by you and Dr. Dobraca?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, these are those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Zujo, let me first direct you and perhaps all of us to the first three documents which are attached to it, which are tabbed as A, B, and C.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again, Mr. President, Exhibit C is Dr. Zujo's autopsy report in the original language. The same report in English is found at Tab A, and that report in French is found at Tab B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I know -- Dr. Zujo, it's up to you, I know that, or I believe that you've brought the same reports yourself in your blue binder there, and if you wish to refer to your own copies of those, I think the Trial Chamber may permit you to do that.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So looking at this document, Dr. Zujo, let me just ask you, is this a report that's related to an examination and findings regarding a body that was subsequently identified as that of Nenad Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this report that we're looking at here, was this then submitted to an investigating Judge with the high court in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you to summarise for us a number of the points that are addressed in this report. First of all, if you can tell us the date and the location in which the exhumation of this body took place. The date and the location of the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: On the orders of the investigating Judge of the cantonal court in Mostar, the team, including Dr. Dobraca and myself with assistants, on the 30th of March, 1998 conducted the exhumations at the Lisak park in Mostar. And under number 5, after the entire procedure had been completed, the body was identified as Nenad Harmandic, born 1947.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, let me just ask you, could you state again the name of the place, the location where the exhumation occurred. I'm not sure we got it correctly.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: It was a park called Lisak, in the Lisak park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My version of the report indicates that the place is called Liska Park, Liska Park. I believe.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Liska, yes, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that the body subsequently identified as that of Mr. Harmandic had been identified initially as number 5. Was that because there were other bodies or body parts that were also exhumed from that location at the same time?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Each corpse was given a number. Since those were individual graves, corpse individually buried, each corpse and each site of exhumation was given a separate number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go directly to what you've mentioned as corpse number 5, or the one that was subsequently identified to be that of Nenad Harmandic. In looking over your report, could you inform the Trial Chamber, please, generally, of your findings in terms of the condition of the body at the time that you examined the body, particularly any apparent injuries which you found during the course of your examination.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: The corpse was completely skeletonised, which means that the soft tissues and internal organs had totally disappeared due to disintegration. And after exhumation, the corpse was transported to the mortuary of the municipal cemeteries at Sutine, where we proceeded with forensic processing. In the course of that processing, we first made a description of all the objects, that is, clothing on the corpse, and we found remains of blue jeans, a leather trouser belt, a remnant of one moccasin, an oblong lighter. That's all we found. And the corpse was wrapped in an army blanket. When we finished with the description of the corpse and all the objects we found with it, we proceeded with the medical processing, which includes an estimate of the age based on certain parameters such as seams, pelvic bones, the collar bone, and the ribs. Then we determined the length of the body, and we also measured the cranium, the length of the femur, and the length of the bone in the upper arms. And we arrived at an average height of this corpse of 182 to 183 centimetres, although according to literature, you can always add another 5 centimetres to the determined value. And the margin of error is 2 centimetres. As for injuries, we found a round hole in the left cheek bone, a fracture of the right shin, fracture of the pelvic bones, fracture of the right ulna, fractures of the left shoulder blade and collarbone, and fractures of the upper and the lower jaws, between the third and the fourth teeth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, excuse me. If you don't mind, I'd like to stop you there and ask you some questions about what you've just been saying. Specifically in respect of the injuries that you've started to mention. First of all, and before I do that, I should ask you, were you able to make an estimate of the approximate age of the corpse at the time of death?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Our finding says that the age was about 45 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, then you began to mention a number of fractures, and I would like to ask you about those first. You mentioned a fracture of the right shin. That's the word that was given to me in English. The shin. Is that bone also called the fibula?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Yes, that is the bone of the shin or the fibula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just, just so we all know, the location -- I think we all know. Could I just say is that one of the two bones of the lower leg, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: In the lower leg, we have the tibia and the fibula. This fibula is slightly behind the tibia. It is much thinner. It is a very thin bone, and its function is not so important, although -- in fact, it's not so important as that of the tibia, of the thicker bone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a fracture of the right ulna. And could you tell us the location of the ulna in the body.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: It is one of the bones of the lower arm. We have the radius bone or the thumb bone, and below it, we have the ulna or the elbow bone because it makes up the elbow. So we have the thumb bone and the elbow bone in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As someone who has -- is an expert in forensic medicine, a fracture of the ulna, as you've described, does that have any particular significance to you in the course of your examination?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Such an injury, an isolated injury without the fracture of the thumb bone, is usually due to the bluntness of the object used. Where we have a fall and one falls on the hand, the fracture is usually just below the lower wrist, and it is then a fracture of both bones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the manner in which the ulna was fractured on this particular specimen, what, if anything, does that tell you about the manner in which the fracture was -- the manner in which the fracture occurred?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Most frequently, it occurs when the arm is protruding in front of the body, when it is -- when this elbow bone is facing the offender, the person inflicting the blow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the arm would have been raised in such a fashion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, that calls for extreme speculation. I object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, we are not in this field. We know nothing about those terms. We are eager to hear the cause of that injury. And in this courtroom, I must confess, I learn something new every day. You may proceed, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I could rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just say to you, this is an expert witness, and the tradition with an expert witness is he is given the respect of the Court and you can lead him. Ask him, "Is this a common injury in defensive injuries?"

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my question, or the direction, Dr. Zujo. The location of the arm, is it an indication of a defensive reflex, perhaps? You mentioned already, I believe, an offender, the arm facing the offender. Do you mean by that to suggest that there is a reflexive -- or a defence reflex that would have put the arm in that position?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that the arm was in front of the body, and of course, I can't tell you whether it was a defensive movement or not, but the arm was raised in front of the body and the elbow bone was facing the attacker. That is, the person who inflicted the injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this type of injury consistent with or typical of an injury sustained as a defensive reflex?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, I believe that you also mentioned additional fractures to the pelvic bones, left shoulder blade, and collarbone, and also the lower jaw. And we'll talk about the upper jaw fracture in a few moments, but perhaps you could elaborate just a bit in terms of the nature of the fractures of the pelvic bones, the left shoulder blade, collarbone, and also the lower jaw, specifically whether the nature of those -- the locations of those fractures, and what, if anything, additional you can tell us about those.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO
utterances.text: In the course of the autopsy, we found a fracture of the left shoulder blade, so we have a left shoulder blade and the left collarbone here on the same side, that is, of the body; whereas the collarbone, the shoulder blade, and the bone in the upper arm make up the shoulder area. So we have fractures of two of these bones, the collarbone and the shoulder blade, which means that the bluntness of the object used in the attack may cause both of these fractures in just one single blow, in a swing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see we've run over. I apologise for that. Perhaps if you wish, we can break until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll break here. Doctor, I'm afraid we have to bring you back tomorrow morning. And during your stay here in The Hague, please do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. The usher will show you out of the room. We'll resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
